what_happened: A naive full-document re-run of literature-convert.sh (auto/pymupdf4llm) on reynolds_2001's PDF produces markedly lower-quality markdown (pervasive spurious bold-wrapping of nearly every paragraph, only 5-6 detected headings vs the paper's 17 sections, a spurious Tesseract OCR fallback on page 0) than the existing hand-curated sec01-sec10 files that were migrated from an older, pre-literature-convert.sh pipeline. A literal reading of the task's 'converted sections present in Literature/' deliverable could lead an implementer to rerun the whole-document converter and silently regress sections 1-4/9-16's established quality. The correct approach (confirmed workable) is a surgical splice: convert only the missing section span, hand-fit 4 new per-section .md files to the neighbors' house style, and insert matching chunks.json entries -- never regenerate the whole document.

Confirmed via chunks.json token_count values (e.g. sec04/section-9 = 3894 tokens, sec08/section-14.3 = 862 tokens, both far outside literature-chunk.sh's 512-token target and sometimes its 1024 atomic-block cap) that this document's existing chunking convention is ONE CHUNK PER PAPER SECTION regardless of size, not literature-chunk.sh's token-budget splitting. Also confirmed literature-build-index.sh's manifest consumer only requires a valid chunks.json plus the source_path files it names -- it does not require literature-chunk.sh's own chunk_NNNN.md naming or re-chunking. Together these mean the planned splice (4 hand-authored chunks.json entries + 4 new secNN_*.md files, no literature-chunk.sh invocation) is fully compatible with the existing pipeline and requires no special-casing.

Per-path suite_selection_select returns a real suite for chunks.json (test-literature-build-index.sh), but the SET-level call that validate-artifact.sh performs returns __FULL_SWEEP__ whenever any path in the phase's set is unmapped (here the .md section files). Authoring a Tier Justification from per-path probes produced two 'fabricated claim' warnings; corrected by claiming the sentinel. Probe the whole declared path set at once, not path-by-path.

The research report pre-settled all four strategy decisions (splice not reconvert, no literature-chunk.sh, --global-only rebuild, no sub-index schema change) with evidence from a scratch test run, so the plan phase needed no independent strategy exploration -- only grounding checks (chunks.json shape, Literature-is-a-separate-git-repo, sub-index entry existence) before writing phases.

Discovered during Phase 1 that the plan's premise (sections 5-8 missing content requiring fresh PDF reconversion) was only half right: the paper's sections 5-8 text already exists verbatim, in house style (## headings, Lemma/Definition/Theorem bold markers, PROOF/qed blocks), physically embedded in the tail of sec03_47-equivalence-results-there-are-two-equ.md. The gap is purely an INDEXING gap: literature-build-index.sh's FTS content_preview truncates to the first 500 words of each chunk's source file, and sec03's §5-8 text (its own chunk is titled only '§4.7-4.8') falls past that word-500 cutoff, so it was never searchable even though the bytes exist on disk. This let Phase 1 skip the literature-convert.sh scratch-PDF-reconversion + hand-fit-and-diff step entirely -- the four new section files were produced by a direct, byte-exact line-range extraction from the existing sec03 file (verified line-boundary-clean at each '## §N.' heading), eliminating the plan's stated #1 risk (a hand-fitting transcription error) since no new text was authored or converted.
